mechanism_narrative: A continued recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT over the next four weeks will pull weekday foot traffic back into commercial districts and raise RETAIL_REC relative to the previous four weeks. The signal is strongest if both series keep moving up together from their current depressed levels.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT each increase for at least two consecutive weekly observations.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while TRANSIT remains suppressed, discretionary shopping shifts toward local, lower-trip retail and lifts RETAIL_REC within one to two weeks. The mechanism weakens when residents do not substitute away from commuting and out-of-home errands.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -15 and RESIDENTIAL remains above +8 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve within 14 days after the TRANSIT and RESIDENTIAL threshold condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A fresh decline in PARKS mobility after a brief rebound indicates renewed distancing behavior that spills into retail visits and pushes RETAIL_REC lower over the next month. This will fail if park use keeps recovering instead of reversing.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by at least 5 points week-on-week after a prior weekly increase
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days after PARKS posts the specified reversal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in GROCERY_PHARM relative to WORKPLACES signals essential, neighborhood-based travel rather than discretionary downtown activity, which will hold RETAIL_REC below its prior four-week average over the next week. The effect is short-lived and should disappear if workplace trips rebound first.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises while WORKPLACES remains below -5
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 7 days despite GROCERY_PHARM increasing and WORKPLACES staying below -5.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL eases from its elevated level, consumers spend less time close to home and reallocate trips toward shopping districts, which increases RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks. The signal is weaker if residential stay-at-home intensity does not fall further.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL posts two consecutive weekly declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals policy relaxation or normalization of commuting, and retail visits should follow with a four-week lag. If only one of the two rebounds, the retail effect should be materially smaller.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise at least 3 points above their prior weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next 28 days despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES clearing the rise threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upswing in PARKS during a reopening phase diverts outings toward leisure travel and nearby spending, which lifts RETAIL_REC within four weeks. The effect disappears if park activity weakens again before the month ends.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior four-week mean over the next 28 days while PARKS continues to recover.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM rises at the same time TRANSIT falls, household trips are being concentrated into essential errands rather than shopping districts, which will depress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks. The mechanism fails when transit use rebounds or grocery trips normalize.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 0 while TRANSIT stays below -20
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises within 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM increases and TRANSIT remains below -20.
